Per: Justice Atul Sreedharan

The present Criminal Appeal has been filed by the sole convict Ganesh,
who was aggrieved by the judgment of conviction and sentence dated 20/01/2016 passed by the Court of the II Additional Sessions Judge, Chhindwara in Sessions Case No. 47/2015; whereby, the appellant was tried along with co-accused Vinod, Siyaram, Pancham and Radhelal.

However,
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55489 2 CRA-612-2016 only the appellant herein was found guilty and convicted for the offences under Sections 302 and 201 I.P.C and was sentenced to suffer imprisonment for life and fine of Rs.2,000/-.

This order shall also consider and dispose off Criminal Appeal No. 3372/2018 (State Vs. Vinod and four others).
2. The appellant Ganesh has remained in judicial custody from 05.10.2014 till the date of his conviction on 20.01.2016 and thereafter IS undergoing his sentence as a convict from 20.01.2016.

3. The case of the prosecution is that on 02/10/2014, the mother of the deceased Roshni, whose name is Saroj appeared before the Police Chowki Rawanbada, under Police Station, Parasiya of District Chhindwara and got a report registered to the effect that her 21 years old daughter Roshni started living with the appellant herein since March.
However, the deceased, without telling anyone left on 30.04.2014.

The mother of the deceased thought that the deceased had gone to seek employment as a labourer but after inquiring from relations and not coming to know her whereabouts, she got the missing persons' report registered as 100/2014 pursuant to which the matter was taken into inquiry.
4. On 04/10/2014, the suspect (appellant herein) in police custody told the police that he was in an illicit relationship with the deceased Roshni.

He further stated that the deceased was compelling him to marry her whereas the appellant did not want to enter into matrimony with the deceased and so on 07/04/2014, in the night, the appellant poured kerosene oil over the deceased and set her on fire.
However, as the deceased survived the fire, the appellant put a rope around her neck and strangulated her till she died.

He further states that he with the help of NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:55489 3 CRA-612-2016 his brother Vinod and his friend Radhe, he buried her body near a brick kiln.
As per the prosecution version, the date of the incident is 07/04/2014 which is purportedly based upon the statement given by the appellant herein.
The relevance of this date shall be disclosed at the later part of this order.

5. On the basis of the said information given by appellant Ganesh, the Police went to the site and in the presence of the mother of the deceased and other witnesses, the body of the deceased was recovered.
The mother of the deceased identified the remains as that of her daughter Roshini in the presence of Smt. Rajkumari and Shobha.
At the scene of exhumation itself, Sub Inspector R.B Goswami prepared Dehalti Merg report and Dehati Nalish.
The appellant was taken into custody on 05.10.2014.
6. The post mortem report is Exhibit P-12.
Briefly stated the post mortem was conducted on 05.10.2014 was on the skeletonized remains of the deceased.

There was no skin or organs found on the skeleton and chapped hair was recovered from the skull of the deceased and the cause of death is inconclusive as there was no viscera, the same having decomposed completely.
In the course of investigation the Police recorded the statement of the witnesses, seized artefacts relating to the crime and filed the chargesheet.

7. In paragraph 10 of her cross-examination, this witness states that she had never given any statement in a Court other than the statement which she had given in the case against Deepak under Section 376 of Indian Penal Code registered by the deceased.

However, to a Court question whether she had given a statement before a Magistrate in Parasiya earlier, the witness says that she had indeed given a statement before the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55489 4 CRA-612-2016 Magistrate earlier.
In paragraph 16 of her testimony, the witness says in cross-examination that it is correct to suggest that the deceased had registered a case against Deepak for rape.

In that case she says that she had testified in the Court and that it is correct to state The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Vinod on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123081711/
2 that she is unaware as to whether her daughter had gone six months before and that it is also correct to state that her statement was recorded in the other case registered by the deceased against Deepak on 8th July, 2014.

sentences.text: She further states in her testimony that it is correct to suggest that in her statement in the case against Deepak that she had testified to the effect that Deepak never gave any promise of marriage to the deceased on the basis of which he took her in a vehicle and committed rape with her.
She further states that in that case registered by the deceased against Deepak, she (the witness) had given an affidavit that Deepak was innocent.

In paragraph 19 of her cross-examination, P.W.-1 states that her other daughter Jyoti is still alive and that Deepak against whom the deceased had levelled the charge of rape, is a grandson to the witness in relation.
In paragraph 20 of her testimony this witness has described how Deepak has a political background and that his father Narbad Singh is Member of Bhartiya Janta Party.
She further says that her daughter (deceased) had filed a case against Deepak at Police Station Parasia for the offence of rape.
She also states that it is correct to suggest that this F.I.R was registered by the deceased against Deepak in March, 2014.

She further states that it is correct to suggest that when the deceased was registering this report against Deepak the witness and her husband tried to dissuade her from doing so by telling her that the matter relates to their family.

In paragraph 32, this witness states that it is correct to suggest that the deceased and Deepak in relation were akin to a brother and sister, and that upon the F.I.R being registered, both the families had to suffer loss of face in the society.

She further states that it NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55489 5 CRA-612-2016 is correct to suggest that as she and her husband had refused to keep the deceased in their house and the police took her to the Women Welfare Centre and also states that she does not as to how and when the deceased escaped from the Women Welfare Centre.

In paragraph 23 this witness states that it is correct to suggest that in the Police Station, Parasia the deceased Roshni was told that the entire expenditure relating to her marriage would be looked after and that she should withdraw her complaint.
In paragraph 26 of her testimony she says that after 30.04.2014, there was no interaction between the deceased and this witness.
In paragraph 26, the witness says that it is correct to suggest that before 02/10/2014, this witness had never given a missing person report to the police.

Upon a question being posed by the Court as to why she did not intimate the Police, earlier, the witness says that the accused persons used to tell her that they have got the deceased married off and sometime used to say that deceased was in Gwalior or she was in Jhansi or Indore and that was the reasons why she did not give a report earlier.
She however, states that it is correct to suggest that she had never told the police this fact.
8. P.W.2 is Bhola.
He is father of the deceased.
He says that his daughter Roshni (deceased) had eloped with the appellant.

He further says that the deceased stayed for three months with the appellant and that when she had eloped, they had gone to register a report to the Rawanbada Police Chowki where it was not registered.
Thereafter they went to Parasiya Police Station where the report was registered.
He further stated that even after the report was registered (missing persons) Roshni was seen the company of the appellant and suddenly, she disappeared.
In paragraph 4 this witness states that the police apprehended the appellant and thereafter in custody, he confessed to the crime.

In cross- NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55489 6 CRA-612-2016 examination, this witness also says that it is correct to suggest that the personnel of P.S. Parasia, brought his daughter (deceased)

3 to his house and that he refused to keep his daughter in his house as she was in habit of running away time and again.

sentences.text: In paragraph 10 of his cross- examination the witness states that he knows Deepak and that Deepak is a nephew in relation and, therefore, would be a brother of the deceased in relation.
He further says that the deceased registered a case under Section 376 I.P.C against Deepak.
In paragraph 12 of the cross- examination this witness says that he does not remember how many times deceased had run away from home.

He further says that after having run away from home twice she came back home and for the third time when she ran away, and did not return, then on the report of the witness, the police brought the deceased to his house.

In paragraph 14 of cross-examination this witness says that the appellant herein was in the custody of the police for three days and it was only thereafter the police called this witness and his wife (P.W.1) to the police Station.
9. P.W.-7 is Kavita.
She is a resident of the same village as of the appellant.
She says that she knows the accused persons and that they reside close to her house.

She says that she does not know the deceased Roshni and says categorically that she has never seen any woman in the company of the appellant and that she is ignorant about the incident relating to the deceased.
She was declared hostile and cross-examined by the prosecution, yet she has stood by what she has stated in her chief.
This witness's statement was taken on two separate dates.
On 15.4.2015, this witness has stated that she does not know the deceased and neither has seen the appellant in the company of any woman.

When she is further examined on 29.06.2015 where she was called for further examination by the prosecution, she does a volteface by stating that she NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:55489 7 CRA-612-2016 knows Roshni and she heard cries coming from the house of the appellant and that the deceased Roshni was shouting "do not beat me"
and that in the statement that she had given in chief on the earlier occasion on 15.4.2015 was not correct.
As regards this witness she is ex facie unreliable as on two different dates she was given two sets of facts relating to the incident.
10. P.W.-8 Guddu was one of the witnesses to the 27 memorandum of the appellant.
He has been declared hostile.
He says that he was witness to the exhumation of the body and that the police got some documents signed by him in Thana.

However, he categorically says that in his presence the appellant was never questioned by the Police and that it is wrong to suggest that the appellant, in his presence told the police that he has buried the deceased in the brick kiln behind his house.
Likewise, is the statement of Rahul Chouhan who is also witness to the seizure memo.

He has also turned hostile and stated that no one was arrested in his presence and that no one was questioned or inquired by the Police in his presence and neither did the appellant make a statement to the fact that the body of the deceased is buried in the brick kiln behind his house.

11. The rest of the witnesses are of no consequence with regard to the relationship that existed between deceased and the appellant and neither are they indicative of any motive that the appellant may have borne to murder the deceased.

Exhibit P.W-19 is the site-map prepared by P.L. Malokhya, who is P.W.12 in this case, which The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Vinod on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123081711/
4 reflects that the house of the appellant is 160 ft. away from the place from where the body of the deceased was interred.

sentences.text: 12. The defence has got a document exhibited on which is pivoted the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55489 8 CRA-612-2016 entire narrative of the prosecution which could be destroyed.
The said document is Exhibit D-8.
This is the 164 statement of the deceased recorded before the Judicial Magistrate in Crime No. 162/2014 for offences under Section 363, 366, 376 (2) (d), 506 and 190 I.P.C.
This was the case that was registered by the deceased against Deepak.
It would be necessary to translate this entire document to understand its import.
The prosecutrix/deceased states that she has studied till class XI and is a resident of village Shankargarh.
Near her house, resides Deepak Bawariya S/o Narbad Bawariya.
Deepak Bawariya was in relationship with her for two years before and that Deepak used to tell her that he would marry her.

Thereafter Deepak Bawariya, one day, called her at 10 p.m and took her in his Xylo Vehicle to the bye-pass road in Parasiya and near the stadium kept her for three to four days and continuously raped her during that time.
One day she told Deepak Bawariya to marry her upon which Deepak refused to do so and told her that he would not marry her and further told her to she could do whatever she wanted.
Deepak Bawariya's father Narbad Bawaria works in W.C.L, who told her to take Rs.50,000/- and withdraw the complaint that she had preferred against his son.
She further says that her parents are also against her and they say that she has a loose character.
She further says that her parents have given it in wiring to the Court that she is a girlsof loose character, on the basis of which Deepak Bawariya got bail.
She says that her parents have thrown her out of the house that she was living with a friend of hers.

Deepak Bawariya is said to have committed rape with her continuously for two years, pursuant to which she conceived once;
upon which Deepak Bawariya gave her some pills.
She further says that Deepak Bawariya threatens her that once he comes out of the jail he would not let her live.

She says that she has given a written report at Thana Parasiya against Deepak Bawariya and she says NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:55489 9 CRA-612-2016 that she has also been examined by the doctor.
13.

Interestingly, this statement u/s. 164 Cr.P.C was recorded before the Magistrate on 03.05.2014,
while the entire prosecution case is that she was murdered on 07.04.2014.

This 164 Statement of hers destabilises the entire prosecution case which reflects that as on 07.04.2014, the deceased was still alive as she gave her statement before the Magistrate's Court under Section 164 Cr.P.C in the case against Deepak a months after she was presumably murdered.
WHEN WAS ROSHINI MURDERED?
14. As this is a case entirely based on circumstantial evidence, the date on which the offence took place assumes significance.

The consistent case of the prosecution is that Roshini was murdered by the appellant at his home on 07/04/2014 first, by setting her on fire and when that did not kill her,
the appellant strangulated Roshini with a rope and the with the help of co- accused persons (since acquitted) buried Roshini's body about one hundred and sixty feet from his house, near a brick kiln.
This narrative of the prosecution is from derived from the 27 memoranda of the appellant.

It is also relevant to mention here that PW1 Saroj (mother of Roshini), PW2 Bhola Bavaria (father of The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Vinod on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123081711/
5 Roshini), PW 10 Narbad Bawariya have testified that the appellant has killed Roshini in the manner mentioned above.

sentences.text: 15. PW1 says that the appellant told the police that he set Roshini on fire and then strangulated her.
Her information regarding the manner in which Roshini died in based on the account of the appellant who allegedly told the police in his statement u/s. 27 of the Evidence Act.
She has no personal knowledge of how Rashini died.
She is not an eye witness.

16. When PW 1 is asked as to how many days had passed before she went to NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55489 10 CRA-612-2016 give the missing report to the police, PW1 says in paragraph 9 of her deposition that she gave the report three months after Roshini went missing.
She further says that the police brought Roshini to her house and when PW1 refused to keep Roshini, the police told her that they would take Roshini and place her at the Women's Welfare Centre.
Ex/P6 is the missing person's report 100/2014 at P.S. Parasia, lodged by PW1 on 02/10/2014, in which the witness says that Roshini went missing on 30.04.2014.

if this document is corelated with paragraph 9 of her deposition that she gave the report three months after Roshini went missing, that would mean that the deceased went missing approximately around July 2014.
However, PW1 also says in paragraph 9 that the police brought the deceased to her home, but she refused to keep her.
This could have happened only on 02/10/2014 or 03/10/2014 as the remains of the deceased were disinterred on 04/10/2014.

But, the remains were in a totally decomposed state with only the skeletal remains without any tissues or maggots, which signify complete decomposition which would have taken more than a month from the time of death, which puts to doubt the statement of PW1 where he says that the police had brought the deceased to her home after she had given the missing person report on 02/10/2014 which is an impossibility as the deceased lay buried at that time.

17. As regards the date on which remains were dug out by the police, PW1 says in paragraph 4 of her deposition that the body was taken out on 03/10/2014 and after it was taken out, the police went to her house and informed her and then she went to the site where the body was buried.
However, the prosecution's case is that the body was taken out on 04/10/2014 and that it was taken out in the presence of PW1.

However this witness contradicts herself in paragraph 11 of her deposition wherein she says that the police personnel came to her home around 11:00 o'clock in the morning and she went with them forthwith and it is only after she reached the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:55489 11 CRA-612-2016 site that they started digging.

Thus, the reliability of this witness is very poor and the scene cannot be taken into consideration by this court in order to assess the manner in which the deceased died and the date on which she died.
1 8 . PW2 is Bhola.
He is the father of the deceased and states somewhat similarly as PW1.
He says that Roshini lived for three months with the appellant and he gave a complaint at P.S. Parasiya when she went missing.

He says that even at the time of giving the missing report, Roshini used to be seen with the appellant (which is distinct from living with the appellant), and if she was being seen with the appellant, where was the need for filing a missing report?
This statement in paragraph 3 of his deposition appears to have been made with the intent to show that the deceased was always with the appellant.

In paragraph 4of the deposition, the manner in which the witness has disclosed The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Vinod on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123081711/
6

sentences.text: his knowledge about the appellant having murdered the deceased is based on the information given to the police by the appellant.
19. In paragraph 9, this witness also, like PW1, states that the police had brought the deceased to house but he refused to keep her.
In paragraph 12 he admits that the police brought Roshini to his house after the missing report was made by PW1.

This again puts the date of Roshini being brought back by the police to the house of her parents on 02/10/2014 (the date on which the missing report was filed by PW1) or 03/10/2014, which is an impossibility as her skeletal remain were unearthed on 04/10/2014.
He too admits the suggestion that he knows Deepak who is a nephew to him in relation.

He also admits the suggestion that the deceased had registered a case against Deepak u/s.
376 IPC for rape.
He has how ever denied that the deceased and Deepak were in a physical relationship for six months and that she had conceived from the said relationship.

20. The information relating to the death of Roshini as stated by PW1 and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55489 12 CRA-612-2016 PW2 is from the information given to them by the police and the same is hearsay.

These witnesses have disclosed three parallel hypothesis that goes against the case of the prosecution which are, (a) that the deceased had filed a case u/s. 376 IPC against Deepak, a relation of the deceased and PW1 and 2, and someone who had a motive to kill Roshini but which angle was never investigated, (b) that after they had registered the missing person's report on 02/10/2014 for Roshini, the police brought Roshini to the house of the witnesss but they refused to keep her, and (c) that the police kept the appellant in custody for three days.
PW1 and 2 have not been declared hostile and therefore the statement of these witnesses binds the prosecution.
21. Ex-D/8 which is the statement u/s. 164 Cr.P.C made by the deceased/prosecutrix in FIR No.
162/2014 registered by the deceased against Deepak, her brother by relation, levelling serious charges of abduction, rape and criminal intimidation to murder, was registered at the same Police Station Parasiya as the FIR relating to the murder of the deceased.
If one goes by the 164 statement of the deceased, then Deepak had the strongest motive to kill the deceased.
It is also pertinent to mention here that the deceased has never mentioned the name of the appellant in her statement.
In the 164 Statement, the deceased says she was in a relationship with Deepak and not the appellant.

Most importantly, on the date on which the prosecution says that the deceased was murdered which is 07/04/2014, the deceased was very much alive as she had given the statement u/s. 164 Cr.P.C before the Magistrate on 03/05/2014.

It appears to be the undisputed case of the prosecution that the deceased had registered a case against Deepak u/s. 376 IPC in which the her parents PW1 and 2 sided with the accused and PW1 even gave an affidavit to the Trial Court in favour of Deepak.

22. Thus, on a dispassionate appreciation of the facts it appears that the only piece of evidence against the appellant is the narrative that come from his 27 NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:55489 13 CRA-612-2016 memorandum ad besides that there is no evidence against him.
It also appears that the Deepak who had sufficient motive to kill the deceased was never investigated into.

sentences.text: 7 23. The appeal is allowed and the conviction of the appellant as hereinabove by the Ld. Trial Court is set aside.
He shall be set forth at liberty forthwith, if not wanted in any case.
DIRECTION TO INVESTIGATION BY THE CBI 24.
The police of P.S Parasiya have not conducted a fair investigation into the case and the person against whom the suspicion was the strongest has not even been investigated.
As the suspect Deepak comes from a politically influential family as has come out in the deposition of PW1 and 2, an investigation by a neutral agency like the CBI would be essential.
So, this court directs the CBI to carry out an inquiry at first to see if the case can be reopened and investigated successfully after so many years.
If it is so possible, then it shall proceed in accordance with law.
REFERENCE TO THE LAW COMMISSION OF INDIA 25.
An innocent man has been wrongly convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment and he has already undergone an incarceration of more than eleven years.

This was not as a result of erroneous investigation but a result of malicious investigation where the police instead of proceedings against the strongest suspect has investigated the case in such a manner that Deepak is not prosecuted and the appellant is made the scapegoat.
This court is of the opinion that the Cr.P.C does not presently have any provision for providing support to a person who has been incarcerated for a long time upon malicious or wrongful conviction.
Once this appellant is released from prison after losing eleven years, what support does he have?

None. The worthy law NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:55489 14 CRA-612-2016 commission is requested to examine the possibility to draft a law that would rehabilitate prisoners who have completed their sentence and re-integrate them into the society as the society still holds a prejudice against someone who had a criminal past and so his rehabilitation into the society without any institutional assistance or involvement, is impossible.

26. In view of the foregoing observations Criminal Appeal No. 612 of 2016 is allowed and Cr. A No.
3372 of 2018, the State appeal, stands dismissed in view of what has been held herein above.

As the suspect Deepak comes from a politically influential family as has come out in the deposition of PW1 and 2, an investigation by a neutral agency like the CBI would be essential.
So, this court directs the CBI to carry out an inquiry at first to see if the case can be reopened and investigated successfully after so many years.
If it is so possible, then it shall proceed in accordance with law.
REFERENCE TO THE LAW COMMISSION OF INDIA 25.
An innocent man has been wrongly convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment and he has already undergone an incarceration of more than eleven years.
This was not as a result of erroneous investigation but a result of malicious investigation where the police instead of proceedings against the strongest suspect has investigated the case in such a manner that Deepak is not prosecuted and the appellant is made the scapegoat.
This court is of the opinion that the Cr.P.C does not presently have any provision for providing support to a person who has been incarcerated for a long time upon malicious or wrongful conviction.
